row.statement: The Windows formal-gate failure is very likely a platform problem, not 19 model failures. Evidence is the asymmetry between runners on the same commit: gates-windows failed formal in about 37 seconds with run=19 matched=0 skipped=17 failures=19, while gates-linux spent over 9 minutes inside the same gate step still running. Zero matched rows plus near-instant completion is the signature of expectation rows never binding - a path or platform resolution issue in formal/run-checks.sh - whereas the Linux runner is doing real simulation work. Diagnose the matcher before treating any of the 19 as a genuine failure.

The formal suite behaves three different ways on the same commit, and only one of them is correct. On this WSL host it completes in 28 seconds with run=19 matched=19 skipped=17 failures=0, SUITE PASSED. On windows-latest it completed in about 37 seconds with run=19 matched=0 failures=19 - zero rows bound, which is a matcher or path fault, not 19 model failures. On ubuntu-latest the same gate step has run past 14 minutes without finishing, across three separate runs. Local timing rules out the suite being inherently slow, so the Linux CI behaviour is a hang or an environment stall and must be diagnosed from the completed log once the 60-minute job timeout fires.

row.statement: An audit lane can return narration and no verdict, and the absence of findings can be misread as approval. The cause is the same single-burst limit that governs implement lanes: the prompt supplied only the DIFF, grok decided it needed the full files to judge equivalence, and the burst ended on that intent. row.statement: The mkdir atomicity alternation is REPRODUCED and explained, and it is not a probe defect. Ubuntu 26.04 points /bin/mkdir at uutils coreutils 0.8.0, and that binary loses mutual exclusion in 20 of 40 eight-racer trials (39 violations total). GNU coreutils 9.7 mkdir, installed alongside as gnumkdir, scores 0 of 40 on the identical harness. So the probe is sound and the Rust mkdir is genuinely unsafe as a lock primitive; the alternating atomic/unknown verdicts of the residual were a coin-flip race being sampled once per run, not a tracer or reporting bug. strace never entered into it - the contention sample alone decides this, and this host rejects ptrace anyway.
row.supersede_reason: The original statement claimed to have reproduced the residual alternation. It did not: atomic-versus-unknown is an strace-attach question, and what was measured is unknown-versus-non-atomic from the contention sample. Same symptom shape, different mechanism, and conflating them would have retired a residual that is still open.

row.evidence: mkdir-atomicity-repro.sh: uutils 0.8.0 VIOLATING=20/40 TOTAL_V=39; GNU 9.7 VIOLATING=0/40; atomic verdict is reachable only via the strace path at tool-check.sh:454-492

row.evidence: strace -f on uutils mkdir over an existing dir shows statx(AT_FDCWD, /tmp/sp3) = 0 then write(2, mkdir); GNU shows mkdir(/tmp/sp3, 0777) = -1 EEXIST
row.statement: uutils mkdir is non-atomic because it CHECKS THEN ACTS, and strace proves the mechanism rather than inferring it. On an existing directory uutils 0.8.0 issues statx(path) and returns its own error, never calling mkdir(2); GNU 9.7 calls mkdir(path, 0777) and takes EEXIST from the kernel. A userspace existence test cannot be atomic against a concurrent creator, which is exactly the 20-in-40 violation rate observed. With strace present the probe upgrades mkdir from a coin-flip contention verdict to a stable non-atomic syscall verdict, so the alternation disappears as well.
row.supersede_reason: The statement presented a documented BLOCKER finding as new. The mechanism, the control and the evidence were all already recorded; only the corroborating rate was mine.

row.evidence: before: GATE bats FAIL test_failures=102 with FM_LOCK_UNAVAILABLE on 170 log lines; after apt install strace, flock probes atomic (syscall) and tests/decision-events.bats returns 10/10
row.statement: strace is a load-bearing DEPENDENCY of foreman, not a debugging convenience, and nothing installed it. The syscall evidence class is the only one that can license a lock mechanism as atomic - flavour licenses nothing, contention can license only non-atomic or unknown - so on Ubuntu 26.04, where /bin/mkdir is uutils, a host without strace has NO trusted mechanism and lib/lock.sh fail-closes with FM_LOCK_UNAVAILABLE. That is what 102 local test failures were: not flaky tests and not a regression, but the lock refusing to operate, across 11 files led by watch (35), lane-supervise (14) and wt-merge (10). Installing strace let flock earn an atomic syscall verdict and the failures went away. env/bootstrap-wsl.sh never installed strace and env/tool-check.sh never reported it, so the whole dependency was invisible to both the provisioner and the readiness report.

row.evidence: command -v strace returned nothing; /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope = 1; after apt install strace, strace -f on mkdir produced mkdir(/tmp/sp1, 0755) = 0 and the flock probe returned atomic (syscall)

Once installed it traced without complaint and licensed flock atomic on the first attempt. Whether the origin host genuinely denied ptrace or merely lacked the binary was never distinguished, and it cannot be: both look identical through command -v strace, which is the only test either the probe or the residual ever applied. A missing tool and a forbidden syscall are different problems with the same signature.

row.statement: Passing a prompt through wsl.exe as a shell argument destroys it, and it cost a wasted vendor round. grok returned --single: prompt is empty because the five-part spec contains backticks, quotes and dollar-parens, and the same defect had already killed the first codex council run. It also silently ate a backtick-quoted word inside a python heredoc and mangled awk field references in several diagnostics. The rule that works: write the prompt or script to a FILE and have a small runner read it with a quoted command substitution inside WSL, never inline it in the wsl.exe argument. Any harness driving vendor CLIs across a Windows-to-WSL boundary needs this or it will lose rounds to empty prompts.

row.evidence: GATE bats FAIL test_failures=1 naming tools/repo-hygiene.sh mode=100644; after the fix, chmod -x on a new committed file produces the INFO line and repo-hygiene still exits 0
row.statement: The mode-regression rule I added had a blind spot that shipped and immediately cost a red gate: it compared each changed file against its base mode and SKIPPED any file with no base, so every NEW file was uncovered. tools/repo-hygiene.sh - the file implementing the rule - landed at 100644 and only tests/line-endings.bats caught it, the fifth exec-bit drop of the session. New files now emit INFO rather than a failure, deliberately: the authoritative inventory lives in tests/line-endings.bats and encodes exclusions this rule cannot see, since 105 of 189 tracked shebang files are correctly 100644 because bats files are run by bats rather than executed. A second limitation stated rather than hidden: the rule reads git diff base...HEAD, so it sees committed state only and cannot warn about a staged file before it lands.

The failing test is the exec-bit inventory, and its output shows mode= EMPTY for every offending file - Git Bash on the runner cannot read the index mode the way the test derives it, so every tracked script reads as violating. That is a test-portability defect, not a product defect and not a real exec-bit problem. So flipping FOREMAN_CI_BATS to 1 on gates-windows would turn that workflow red immediately, on one of only two files anyone has ever probed, with 48 more unprobed.

row.evidence: codex audit round 2 differential harness: jq gave [implement,1] and fallback gave [discover,5] for one nested record; jq rc=5 on a trailing comma where the fallback extracted [discover,2]
row.statement: A jq-optional regex fallback for JSON cannot be made correct, and two audit rounds proved it the expensive way. Round 2 fixed every malformed case the architect supplied - unrecognised phase, missing phase, invalid weight, invalid JSON, each refused with a line number - and the auditor then found a class nobody had supplied: the record with a nested object carrying a decoy phase parses as implement/1 under jq and discover/5 under the regex, and a trailing comma that jq rejects is silently accepted. Both are VALID-input divergences, not malformed-input handling. The task file asked for the fallback in so many words, so the fix is a contract change rather than another regex: delete the fallback and require jq, which is already required = true in the manifest and a must tool for hard, full and durable. The general rule: if a spec asks for a parser that cannot be correct, patching it produces a checker that agrees on the cases someone thought of and diverges on the rest - which for a metric is worse than refusing.

Decide: drop formal from the hosted gates and leave it to formal.yml, or drop formal.yml and let the gates own it. Running both on every push is waste, and a 10-minute gate discourages the per-commit gating criterion 3 is meant to establish.

Fix the WSL clock preflight: it reports an empty host clock reading as drift-beyond-threshold. Distinguish could-not-read from measured-drift, and find why the host clock read returns empty under a lane-run invocation on this host. Until then every lane-run round begins with a false drift alert, which trains readers to ignore it.

Re-scope what criterion 2 actually requires, now that the 26 CI failures are triaged to ZERO product defects. 19 were the unbuilt POSIX launcher (fix merged at 8a6ff00, awaiting its first hosted run), 5 are environment-only and pass locally, and 2 are a stale gate fixture predating the three-outcome-verdicts hardening (lane/gate-fixture in flight). Criterion 2 asks for the suite green on three consecutive runs; on this evidence that is a fixture and environment problem, not a debugging problem. Re-measure after the launcher and fixture fixes land before planning any further test work.

The Use-path readiness gate fails OPEN when no probe is available, and this predates the FOREMAN_TOOL_CHECK work. Both before and after, lane-run.sh only enforces LANE_READY when a probe exists: originally guarded on env/tool-check.sh being present, now on the override being set OR that file being present - a strict superset, so the refactor did not weaken it. But in a checkout where env/tool-check.sh is missing and no override is set, a lane spawns with NO readiness check at all and nothing says so. Decide: refuse when no probe can be found (fail closed), or emit a loud NOT-VERIFIED marker. Silently skipping a gate is the failure mode this release keeps finding.

The T2 argv-equivalence test freezes the pre-refactor builder as an IN-TEST COPY (legacy_implement_argv in tests/adapters.bats), not as a call into historical code. The architect verified the copy is faithful to the merge-base builder, and the grok audit approved it while flagging the standing risk: it is sound only while the copy stays independent of the adapters. If a future change edits both the adapters and that helper together, the test becomes circular and asserts nothing. Either add a comment forbidding edits to legacy_implement_argv, or replace it with a check that reads the builder out of git history at the pinned commit.

Identify why the CI bats failure count moved from 12 to 13 on the traps-17 merge, which changed only AGENT_TRAPS.md. Either a docs-structure test reads that file - readme-structure.bats and docs-check.bats are candidates - or the suite has a flaky test. Criterion 2 requires three consecutive green runs and cannot be met while the count moves on a docs-only commit. Compare the per-slice reports of runs 30683976294 and 30684042600 to name the slice that changed.

tests/foreman-setup.bats is flaky on CI: one failure appeared on run 30684042600 and was gone on the next run with no relevant change between. It has 4 tests and its baseline row says 3, so its expected-pass count is already drifting too. Identify the flaky case and its mechanism - read it rather than sampling - before criterion 2 (three consecutive green runs) is attempted. Do not raise the baseline to absorb it.

The CI test artifact cannot name a failing test. tests/run.sh uploads foreman-test-slices.tsv with per-slice pass/fail/skip counts, and the job log carries only the GATE bats summary, so a CI-only failure like the foreman-setup flake cannot be attributed to a case. Capture per-test TAP output as an artifact - or at minimum the not-ok lines - so a runner-only failure is diagnosable without guessing. This blocks obligation 39 and, through it, criterion 2.

Re-freeze the argv equivalence baseline DELIBERATELY. --no-leader on the grok implement path is wanted - grok agent defaults to a shared ~/.grok/leader.sock, a real cross-lane coupling point - so the behaviour change is correct and should stay. What is wrong is that the frozen copy was silently edited to match, voiding the test. Restore legacy_implement_argv to true pre-T2 state and have the test assert equality EXCEPT a declared allowlist of intentional deviations, currently just --no-leader. That keeps the test able to fail while permitting deliberate change, which is what the guard comment on main already instructs.

Decide whether the docs-check archive prune should be package-scoped rather than archive-wide. The gate now prunes openspec/changes/archive entirely. Today that is equivalent to a narrow exclude - only one .sh exists under archive and it belongs to a withdrawn package - but 12 of the 13 archived packages are shipped-and-archived rather than withdrawn, so a future script added under one of those would be silently exempted. grok audited APPROVED and flagged this low: a package-scoped exclude would match the stated reason more tightly if archive-wide exclusion is not the lasting policy.

bugeventlog.md has two events both titled Event 3 - a watchdog with two ... at lines 1868 and 1917, surfaced once MD024 was configured to fire only on same-parent duplicates. A defect log with two entries sharing a number cannot be cited unambiguously. Renumber the later one or merge them, and check whether the duplication means an event was recorded twice.

Decide when docs-check becomes an actual CI gate. It is absent from ci-local.sh gate list, so criterion 9 is unenforced by the workflows that run on every push. Adding it now turns gates-linux red because markdownlint (92) and the comments gate (57) both still fail. Sequence it after those reach zero, or add it in shadow first - but do not leave criterion 9 depending on a gate that never runs.

Fixing the bugeventlog triplication is a prerequisite for Plan 5 Tier 1, not merely a doc-sprint nit. regression-harness-tiers tasks 2.2/2.3 enumerate every distinct failure class from bugeventlog.md and seed one golden round per class, and task 2.6 compares failure classes against rounds. A triplicated entry inflates the class count and would seed three rounds for one failure. Land the dedup before Tier 1 enumeration runs.

Vendor diagnostic text is DROPPED on the verdict-rejection path. adapter_result_verdict emits only _ADAPTER_RESULT_ERROR; a marker written to the vendor stderr file does not appear in the output. The test covering this is named "verdict extraction preserves the stream carrying payload or failure", so the name overclaims what the code does. Either preserve the vendor stderr on the reject path (preferred - the name states the intended contract) or rename the test. Confirmed by control, not just by audit.

grok-multiround.sh decides success with a git-status-porcelain digest that this session demonstrated is blind in two ways, and it requires an undocumented clean-worktree precondition. evidence-contracts owns the replacement predicate (lib/evidence.sh) and vendor-multiround.sh per vendor-adapter-contract T5, so do NOT patch the predicate in place here. Until that lands: dispatch lanes only into clean worktrees, and treat any EMPTY-BURST verdict on a dirty tree as unproven. The 2026-08-01 fix at 895c44e improved the DIAGNOSIS on the failure path, not the soundness of the detection.

openspec task files are not being ticked as work lands: vendor-adapter-contract shows 0 of 42 done while T1-T4 are implemented, verified and merged. Package completion is therefore unmeasurable, which matters because the release counts packages. Update tick state from EVIDENCE ONLY - a command whose output proves each task - and leave anything unproven unticked with a note, rather than ticking a section because its heading was worked on.

audit-verdict.bats test 9 ("current UNVERIFIED in_progress attempt is published before codex finishes") fails in CI at line 331 on [ "$after" = "$before" ], baseline 26 actual 25. This is the second byte-equality-over-a-generated-artifact assertion to fail only under CI load, alongside foreman-setup test 2. Both compare a hash or a file before and after an operation expected to be a no-op. Diagnose whether the artifact embeds a timing- or ordering-derived value rather than raising the baseline.

Diagnose test 9 from CI evidence rather than from local reproduction, which has failed twice. The verdict artifact carries time-derived fields (ended_at, duration_s) and an evidence.attempt counter, so any second write is identifiable from the artifact itself. A diagnostic block was added to the failing path (lane/diag9) that dumps the before/after shas, the post-kill artifact and the audit-run log tail into the TAP stream, WITHOUT weakening the assertion. Read the next red gates-linux run before proposing any fix.

The multiround exclusion is ROOT-ONLY: the regex is ^SPEC-[^/]*\.md$, so d/SPEC-notes.md is counted as work and a notes-only round gets a false SUCCESS. Confirmed identical in the pre-change code, so it is pre-existing and was preserved deliberately. Do NOT simply widen it: a lane whose real deliverable is docs/SPEC-foo.md would then be excluded and reported EMPTY-BURST, converting a false positive into a false negative. Decide whether the exclusion should key on the caller-staged spec PATH (known at dispatch) rather than on a filename pattern. Owned by evidence-contracts.

Gitignored paths are invisible to the multiround evidence predicate: a worker writing only into an ignored directory is reported EMPTY-BURST despite doing real work. Confirmed by control. git status never reports ignored paths, so no status flag fixes this; the declared-deliverable set does, because content records are computed per declared path regardless of status. This is the argument for wiring the declared deliverable set (evidence-contracts T2.6) rather than relying on enumeration.

Audit every other Windows-interop call for the same cwd sensitivity now that the repo lives under /root. The clock preflight was found by accident because it printed on every round; a silent interop call would not announce itself. Candidates: agy invocations, install.ps1 paths, the launcher tool-check, anything reaching /mnt/c binaries. The rule to apply: an interop call must set its own Windows-resolvable cwd in a subshell rather than inheriting the caller.

tests/lane-ownership-harness.sh reports PASS=21 FAIL=3 HARNESS FAILED on main, and has done so independently of any change made today (verified identical before and after the shdoc commit). It is a .sh harness rather than a bats file, so it does not appear in the bats tally that criterion 2 tracks, and its 3 failures have been invisible to the release gate. Identify them and decide whether they are encoded known-failures or real regressions before the tag.

The comments gate needs a second pass: 31 undocumented functions remain across ten files - tools/ci-local.sh 8, tools/lanectl.sh 6, audit-run.sh 5, grok-multiround.sh 3, graph-project-harness.sh 2, lib/metrics-lint.sh 2, lib/evidence.sh 2, wt-new.sh 1, graph-project.sh 1, env/tool-check.sh 1. Three of the grok-multiround.sh entries were introduced by the evidence-wiring merge a54c51b today, so new code is arriving undocumented faster than the gate is being cleared.

Decide the doc-scope question for docs/superpowers/plans/**: 30 of the 67 markdownlint findings are in one dated plan file, 2026-07-31-v029-tranche-a1-recording-instruments.md, including all 10 MD010 hard-tab findings whose column positions (659:24, 659:30, 660:24, 660:28) look like columnar data of exactly the kind a blanket tab fix destroyed once already. The config already exempts docs/research/** and docs/evidence/** on the stated principle that editing an archive to satisfy a linter falsifies it, and dated plan records arguably have the same status. This is the owner call - do NOT add the ignore silently, and do NOT blanket-fix the tabs.

Three test slices carry permanent non-PASS budget/baseline verdicts that do not fail the run: tests/launcher.bats (skip 11 vs budget 10, pass 3 vs baseline 4), tests/nats-bridge.bats (skip 12 vs budget 0, pass 0 vs baseline 12), tests/adapters.bats (no budget or baseline row at all -> ERROR). Two consequences. First, the launcher row moved because the pidns capability guard added an eleventh legitimate skip, so its budget and baseline are simply stale by one. Second, a verdict that is permanently FAIL or ERROR without gating anything teaches readers to ignore it - the same lesson as the false clock-drift alert. Either make these verdicts gate, or correct the rows so they mean something. This is obligation 28 with measured numbers attached.

row.blocker: Resolved by Foreman PR 10 merge 09e0715; exact-main Linux run 30805814811 passed the 12-test NATS slice.
row.statement: nats-bridge.bats carries 12 skips against a skip budget of 0 and 0 passes against a baseline of 12, permanently, because nats-server/nats are not installed on the CI runner. Deliberately left uncorrected when the launcher and adapters rows were fixed: changing it means deciding whether twelve permanently skipped tests are acceptable for the release, which is a scope judgement for the owner rather than a stale number. Either install nats on the runner, or set the budget to 12 and the baseline to 0 with that decision recorded.

tools/ci-local.sh reports CI-LOCAL RESULT FAIL on this developer host for an environment reason: GATE openspec FAIL /usr/local/bin/openspec not executable. It passes in CI (packages_valid=34). A local gate runner that always fails trains its readers to ignore it - the same lesson as the false clock-drift alert and the permanently-FAIL policy rows. Either make the local openspec resolvable or have the gate report NOT-AVAILABLE rather than FAIL when the tool is absent.

bats has NEVER run on the Windows runner. gates-windows now opts out explicitly with FOREMAN_CI_BATS=0 because bats is not provisioned there (rc=127). Provisioning it and running the suite on Windows is real, unscoped work: the suite has 46 files and has only ever been exercised on Linux and WSL, so the first Windows run should be expected to surface platform failures rather than pass. Decide whether Windows suite coverage is in scope for v0.2.9 or later, and note that criterion 3 currently means "both gates green" with the Windows gate NOT running the suite.

AMENDS obligation 51, which was closed prematurely. The multiround spec exclusion must KEEP the root-level SPEC-*.md pattern: it is the manufactured-artifact guard pinned by tests/grok-multiround.bats test 4, and replacing it with an exact-staged-path rule reintroduced the SPEC-NOTES.md false SUCCESS and turned gates-linux red for three runs. The exclusion is now the UNION of both rules (467e6d3). The case the path rule was meant to fix - a lane whose genuine deliverable is a root-level SPEC-*.md being reported EMPTY-BURST - remains KNOWINGLY unfixed: it is hypothetical here while the notes-file defect is recorded as having happened. If it ever occurs, key the exclusion on the dispatch-time declared deliverable set rather than widening or narrowing a filename pattern.

Criterion 6 requires every measurement fresh at the tag WITH its re-run command. 9 of 47 recorded measurements pin a specific CI run id (e.g. "gh run download 30686798678 && grep -c ^ok foreman-test-tap.log"), so re-running them reproduces a HISTORICAL number rather than a current one - they cannot be refreshed, only re-read. Affected: the gates-linux/gates-windows pass, fail and skip counts and ci_suite_failures_launcher_caused. Before the tag, re-record these with a parameterised command that resolves the NEWEST completed run (gh run list --limit 1 --json databaseId) or with the local equivalent (bash tests/run.sh), and retire the pinned rows. The other 38 are re-runnable as written.

Before merging a change to any script under skills/foreman/scripts, enumerate its test drivers mechanically: grep -rln "<script-name>" tests/ and run every file that matches, not a hand-picked list. Two regressions today (spec-path exclusion, T7 claude removal) reached main because the failing test file was not in the set I chose to run, while every suite I did run was green. Consider adding this to the merge checklist or, better, a helper that prints the driver set for a changed path.

T7 is INCOMPLETE: skills/foreman/scripts/wt-new.sh still provisions a claude vendor-home dir (lines 8, 172, 267) and tests/vendor-isolation.bats:162 asserts it. Three of the four advertising sites were removed (lane-run vendor map, lane-queue group, tool-check --lane); the fourth was missed because my spec named it as wt-new.sh:106-109 and the real lines are 172/267, so the probe found nothing there. The directory is now dead weight - nothing can use it, since lane-run refuses the vendor - but it still advertises support. Remove the claude vendor-home provisioning and update that test, or record why it stays.

Criterion 4 cannot be closed until the unit of "checker" is fixed. Decide whether the negative-control registry is keyed on verdict emission sites (110), owning files (23), or a third unit such as named checker functions, and re-state criterion 4 in that unit. The current text says "~60-80", which matches neither measured unit. Whoever builds the registry must record the unit in the registry file itself so completeness is computable.

Reconciliation lanes must not use FOREMAN_CONFIG=/dev/stdin or any non-seekable stream as a config fixture: cfg_load cannot re-read it, so every cfg_get silently returns its default and the fixture proves nothing. Future lane specs that ask for config-precedence evidence must require a real temporary file and require the fixture contents to be printed alongside the result.

lane/audit-call must not merge until the selected auditor and the invoked auditor are the same vendor. Minimal correct fix: restore a fail-closed refusal when the selected vendor has no invocation path in audit-run.sh, preserving EXIT_MISSING_CLI and reason code missing_cli, and naming the selected vendor. The alternative - making the invocation dynamic by sourcing adapters/$AUDIT_VENDOR.sh and passing "$AUDIT_VENDOR" to adapter_audit_argv - is T4 work (wire both tiers) and larger; either closes the defect, but nothing may merge while ACTUAL_VENDOR can disagree with the process actually run.

Criterion 6 requires every measurement fresh at the tag commit, and the store currently reports fresh=11 STALE=44. There is no mechanism to discharge that: fm-session.py exposes begin/recover/end/fact/measure/obligation/close/project/sidecar/import-sidecar/supersede/retire and no freshness or bulk-recheck subcommand, and "recover" prints only the metric, value, staleness verdict, timestamp and sha - never the stored --command - so the re-run command for a stale measurement cannot even be read from the report a human would consult. Before tagging, either add a subcommand that lists each stale measurement WITH its recorded command (and ideally re-runs it), or retire the stale measurements that no longer bear on the release. Doing this by hand for 44 entries at tag time is how a freshness sweep silently becomes a rubber stamp.

T4 (wire both audit invocation tiers) must remove the dual hardcode that the cross-vendor grok audit flagged as a low finding: audit-run.sh gates on AUDIT_VENDOR == "codex" in one place and independently passes the literal string codex to adapter_audit_argv in another. Correctness currently depends on those two staying aligned by hand, and an edit that changes only one of them silently reopens the selected-vs-invoked mismatch. T4 should source adapters/$AUDIT_VENDOR.sh and pass "$AUDIT_VENDOR", deleting the refusal and the literal together.

Stop writing "commit on the current branch" into codex lane specs. codex exec --sandbox workspace-write cannot run git, so the instruction is unsatisfiable and its presence made me misread four lanes as ignoring the spec. Replace it with an instruction to leave the worktree clean and complete, and have the architect (or a wrapper outside the sandbox) do the commit. If a lane genuinely must commit, it needs a different sandbox mode, which is a separate decision.

BLOCKING on T3/T6 of audit-groundedness-gate: no registered check may leave shadow until the canary is proven against a REAL evaluator. gg_canary_evaluate_fixture is caller-supplied and its only implementation is the test double at tests/gate-ground.bats:22, which keys on basename and reads no semantic field, so CANARY_OK today means "the harness comparison works", not "G1-G9c can fail". Closing this requires a non-double evaluator plus a mutation proof that corrupts or deletes a REAL predicate rather than flipping the doubles GG_TEST_NOOP_CHECK / GG_TEST_WRONG_FOCUS_CHECK env knobs. Until then the two withdrawn T2 checkboxes stay un-ticked.

BLOCKING on T6 (gate integration) of audit-groundedness-gate: gg_canary_run is bound to no gate entrypoint, so acceptance criterion 4 - the canary runs on EVERY invocation before the checker trusts its own result - is not mechanized. The library is source-safe and runs no canary on load, and the test that claims per-invocation evaluation only calls the helper twice and asserts both succeed. T6 must create the choke point. Related: the open-world-enforcing refusal and the no-promotion demotion are cooperative APIs, so a caller reading GG_REGISTRY_MODE directly bypasses both named refusals; the same choke point should force them.

audit-groundedness-gate: a valid but EMPTY registry (blocking_cap=0, header, zero rows) makes the canary vacuous - expected_total=1, only the baseline fixture, zero per-check mutants - so CANARY_OK would mean "baseline matched empty output" rather than "a registered check can fail". gg_canary_run should refuse a registry with zero rows as UNVERIFIED with its own reason, on the same fail-closed principle as the short/unreadable/shape-mismatch corpora.

Lane dispatch must not silently reuse a branch name. Two fixes, both cheap: stop discarding the git branch -D exit status in dispatch scripts, and make the branch name unique per dispatch rather than per package. Separately, 34+ stale lane worktrees are registered under /root/fm-wt and hold branch names hostage; wt-cleanup.sh exists and should be run against the merged ones before the tag.

When the architect commits a codex lane worktree, check file modes first: a bash-shebang file created in the sandbox can land 100644 and turn gates-linux red, as lib/audit-call.sh did at 74d7a33. Add a mode check to the pre-merge routine - the derivation already exists in tests/line-endings.bats and can simply be RUN rather than reimplemented.

Any CI step whose job is to REPORT a failure rather than gate on one must disable errexit explicitly. GitHub runs shell: bash with -eo pipefail, so such a step is destroyed by the first failure it was written to observe, and continue-on-error hides that as non-fatal. Silence from a diagnostic step is not evidence of a clean result; a diagnostic must print something on every path. Review existing informational steps for the same shape before the tag.

audit-groundedness-gate MEDIUM from the T3 audit: an empty registry is not fail-closed. Unreadable JSON yields GG_CHECK_FIXTURE_INVALID and an unimplemented gg_check_$id yields GG_CHECK_UNIMPLEMENTED, both correct, but an empty GG_REGISTRY_IDS only triggers a reload of GG_DEFAULT_REGISTRY, and a registry that loads successfully with ZERO rows is accepted: the evaluate loop then runs zero times and returns 0, so CANARY_OK means "no checks ran" rather than "no violations found". gg_canary_run should refuse a zero-row registry with its own UNVERIFIED reason, on the same principle as the short and shape-mismatched corpora.

audit-groundedness-gate MEDIUM from the T3 audit: G1 declares repository_head among its required_inputs but its predicate tests membership in changed_paths only. gg_check_require can therefore mark G1 unevaluated when repository_head is absent, while a citation genuinely outside the diff goes unflagged - a silent under-fire relative to the declared inputs, and a contradiction of G1 own zero-false-positive rationale, which says "absent from the complete diff AND repository path sets". Either use repository_head in the predicate or remove it from required_inputs and amend the rationale.

When a script that documented itself as side-effect-free gains a mutation, re-derive its safety properties rather than editing the sentence. foreman-setup.sh changed from "mutates nothing on disk" to building a launcher; the doc was honestly updated but the four properties that purity had been providing for free - atomic replacement, a guarded test seam, parse-before-mutate, and unchanged signal coverage - were not added. Treat the removal of a purity claim as a checklist trigger, not a comment edit.

row.blocker: Resolved as an active blocker: current main and the Council PR stack have consecutive green Linux gates. The cited v0.2.9 criterion is withdrawn.
row.statement: Criterion 2 requires the suite to pass on three CONSECUTIVE runs and criterion 3 requires both gates green on main. Neither can be certified while gates-linux flaps: the observed pattern is success at 7ad8a30, failure at 124c030, success at a4aa473, success at 22fe2a3, failure at aa471c8. The flake is the mkdir atomicity probe, now being fixed. Before ticking criterion 2, count consecutive green runs AFTER that fix lands, not before - the current green runs are interleaved with red ones and prove nothing about consecutiveness.

Pre-merge verification must include the two things WSL cannot show. First, file modes as recorded in the index for every new file (obligation 75, already caught one recurrence). Second, any test carrying a wall-clock or resource bound must be identified before merge and its margin stated, because a bound met locally with a small margin will fail on a slower shared runner. Both regressions today were caught by CI rather than by me, and each cost a red main plus a diagnosis cycle. Cheapest implementation: a pre-merge script that prints index modes for new files and greps the changed tests for time-based assertions.

row.blocker: Resolved: gate-ground now passes in the 685-test exact-main Linux aggregate; main is not carrying the three cited known failures.
row.statement: While main is red on the canary cost overrun, every gates-linux run carries three known failures in tests/gate-ground.bats. Any NEW failure must be distinguished from those three before it is attributed to the commit under inspection. This is the exact trap that made me call a six-run red streak a one-run regression earlier today: I read the newest run rather than the first red one. Until the canary-cost fix lands, diagnose by comparing the failing test NAMES against {canary validates exact count, canary evaluates the corpus, mutation proof}, not by the pass/fail verdict.

Every scripted edit-then-commit must gate the commit on its own verification step, with a nonzero exit that stops the script. Today a checklist corruption reached origin because the script printed a verification result and then committed regardless. Pattern to use: compute the check, test it, exit 1 on failure BEFORE git add. Applies to every scratchpad script in this workflow that edits a tracked file.

AMENDS obligation 75. The pre-merge file-mode check must cover MODIFIED tracked files, not only new ones. It was written as a scan of git ls-files -o (untracked), which is where the first two exec-bit regressions came from; the third came from a lane modifying an already-tracked bash script and dropping its mode, which the merge recorded as "mode change 100755 => 100644" and the check never saw. Correct form: run bats tests/line-endings.bats before every merge and act on what it flags - it derives the inventory from a whole-repo shebang property and is exempt from nothing.

OWNER DECISION: Tier 2 task 3.1 ("lock 8-12 specs with seeded defects against a pinned vendor model") requires live vendor runs and therefore real spend, and Tier 2 is required to have no automatic trigger. An autonomous session can build and test the machinery but must not fire it. Decide whether to authorise a Tier 2 baseline run before the tag, or to ship v0.2.9.0 with Tier 2 built-but-never-executed and say so plainly in the release notes. The second is defensible; leaving it ambiguous is not.

Confirm the gates-linux queue drains and yields a verdict on c251a22 or later. Seven runs sat in_progress with all steps concluded for 20+ minutes. If they do not complete, investigate whether anything in the gate path leaves a process alive that holds the runner open after the final step - ci-local.sh:233 detaches the bats run with setsid inside a command substitution, which waits on stdout rather than on the process, so a grandchild that outlives the step is a plausible mechanism worth ruling in or out with evidence rather than reasoning.

Scripted edits to tracked files must write a temp file, assert on its contents, and os.replace it over the original - never open the target for writing directly. A python open(...,"w") that raises on a bad argument truncates the file first, which emptied tests/gate-ground.bats today; only the commit gate prevented the push. This complements obligation 83 (gate the commit on verification): the gate stops a bad commit, but write-to-temp stops the damage.

When merging any lane that ran fm-session.py, discard .foreman/session.db from the lane worktree before committing. The script creates a store wherever it runs, so a lane worktree gains an orphaned one that nothing reads; committing it would place a second divergent store in the repository. The tool already warns about this at runtime - the pre-merge routine must act on the warning.

OWNER DECISION: reword criterion 5. It requires a codex-auditor verdict per package, which cannot be satisfied for any package codex implemented without violating the cross-vendor invariant the release itself now enforces in code. Either reword to "a cross-vendor auditor verdict per package" (the vendor chosen by ac_select_auditor, recorded in the verdict), or state that codex-implemented packages are audited by grok and the criterion means the AUDIT happened rather than that a specific CLI produced it. Leaving it naming codex makes the criterion unsatisfiable by construction.

Criterion 5 needs a defined artifact before it can be counted. audit-run.sh writes audit-verdict.json per RUN, and this session audited per LANE, but nothing in the tree defines what a per-PACKAGE verdict is or where it lives. Define that artifact (path, schema, which run produced it) and then count it; until then any "N of 34 packages audited" figure is unfounded, including the 30-of-34 grep proxy I took, which only shows the package name appears somewhere under docs/evidence.

Decide what foreman does about uutils mkdir now that it is proven non-atomic. lib/lock.sh is fail-closed and correctly refuses an untrusted mechanism, so nothing is silently broken - but on a stock Ubuntu 26.04 host BOTH mechanisms fail to earn trust (mkdir non-atomic by contention, flock unknown because ptrace is denied), which leaves the lock unusable rather than merely unproven. Options: prefer GNU mkdir when gnu-coreutils is installed and pin the binary in the trust record rather than trusting the name on PATH; or license flock by a non-strace route so it can carry the lock on hosts without ptrace. The residual entry that says the alternation could not be reproduced locally should be replaced with fact 214.

OWNER DECISION: disposition of the four scope-call packages. RESUME-2026-08-01.md attributes this to obligations 76 and 77, but those are the CI errexit rule and the groundedness empty-registry defect - no obligation ever recorded this decision, so it existed only in a prose doc. wsl-seam-doctrine is NOT obsolete as a whole: only its Docker item is direction-reversed (the repo installs native docker-ce while the task asks for a Docker Desktop doctrine plus an uninstall-native warning) and its exec-bit item was superseded by tests/line-endings.bats; three items remain live and cost under a day. spec-triage-gate, foreman-discover-lane and workload-fit-accounting are the empirical-workloads trio A, B and D of the 2026-07-19 plan, whose sibling C (captured-facts-convergence) has ALREADY LANDED - so parking B leaves C referencing a discover lane that will never be built, which any deferral or withdrawal must state.

AMENDS obligation 84. The pre-merge file-mode check must not derive its inventory from a bash-shebang property, because that misses every other interpreter. fm-session.py is python, was 100755 on main, lost the bit to a Windows-side edit, and tests/line-endings.bats test 3 passed anyway - it only covers bash. The check that actually works is a direct index-mode comparison of every file the branch changed against the base: git diff --name-only BASE...HEAD, then git ls-tree BASE vs git ls-files -s per path. That is interpreter-agnostic and covers modified tracked files, which is what obligation 84 asks for and what the shebang derivation cannot give. Seven files on this branch lost mode 100755 in total; six were caught by the gate and the seventh only by the mode audit.

Tier 2 trigger-absence proof is narrower than its wording. tests/tier2-trigger-scan.sh defaults its targets to .github, superpowers/hooks, foreman/scripts, tools, env and the two install scripts - it does NOT scan tests/ or the repository root. Meanwhile tests/tier2-compare.bats invokes the collector with --acknowledge-paid-vendor-calls at lines 401 and 415, on every commit, which the scan cannot see by construction. No money is spent because the adapter passed is a fixture, so the safety property that actually holds is the adapter you pass is a fixture, NOT the acknowledgment flag is absent. Tier 2 cannot honestly compute its own budget check. tests/tier2_collect.py:72 requires the adapter to return a numeric non-negative cost_usd and offers no unavailable path, while lib/telemetry.sh records that all three vendors surface no reliable per-round usage and writes source unavailable with the numerics ABSENT under the standing rule that an absent figure is data and never zero. So any real Tier 2 run would compute budget_breach from a number the adapter invented. Give the adapter contract an unavailable path and let the budget check record not_evaluated, or define a documented token-based estimator and mark it source estimated. Until then the declared 18 USD ceiling is undefended and uncheckable.

v0.3.0+ DIRECTION, not this release: make TypeScript with Effect the single Foreman language and retire Python. Owner-stated 2026-08-01. Council already is TypeScript + Effect 3 with a runtime-free event-sourced domain, so the monolanguage direction is coherent rather than speculative - it makes the deliberation plane and the execution plane one stack instead of two. Evidence gathered today that bears on it: the earlier objection to TypeScript for the session store was dependency cost, and the owner voided that premise - the host always provisions, so promoting node/bun is a manifest row, not a risk. bun is already pinned and compiles foreman-launch, and bun:sqlite would give a zero-runtime-dependency store. What survives as a real consideration is BUILD steps versus INSTALL steps: fm-session.py must run on a cold host during recovery before anything is built, so a compiled recovery tool needs the binary shipped or built in bootstrap. Not scoped here; recorded so the decision starts from measured ground rather than from scratch.
